title: Traffic Shift Circuit KPI Runbook
content:
Purpose and scope:
This runbook captures the operational wiring, KPI tracking, and circuit-breaker thresholds for staged traffic shifts (canary -> ramp -> full) for product launches and model rollouts. Designed for product-ops + SRE + release engineering to use during daytime or after-hours rollouts.

Summary (one-liner):
Define exact stop/slow/rollback triggers, what metrics to observe, and who acts when thresholds are hit. Keep lightweight — point to monitoring dashboards for raw numbers.

Phases and traffic targets:
- Phase A (Canary): 1% traffic for 30m — sanity checks and smoke tests.
- Phase B (Ramp-1): 10% traffic for 60m — observe latency p50/p95, error spike, and functional correctness checks.
- Phase C (Ramp-2): 50% traffic for 90m — hold and validate traffic shaping, caches, and autoscaling behavior.
- Phase D (Full): 100% traffic with extended monitoring and post-launch watch for 6 hours.

Primary KPIs to monitor (owner in parens):
- Request success rate (SRE): target >= 99.8% over 5m window.
- Client-visible latency (p50/p95/p99) (Product): p95 target < 250ms for short requests; p99 < 1.5s.
- Token throughput per GPU (Infra): expected baseline +-10% from benchmark.
- Cost per 1k tokens (Finance/Product): track delta vs baseline.
- Model quality regressions (ML/Product): A/B eval set score drop > 1.5% (relative) triggers investigation.
- Queue/backlog length and queue time (SRE): queue > 200ms median or rising trend > 10%/10m is a concern.
- Error mode split (SRE/Product): 5xxs vs 4xxs breakdown — large 5xx spike is critical.

Circuit-breaker thresholds (immediate actions):
- Stop and rollback to previous variant if any of the following sustained for 3 consecutive 1m windows:
  * Success rate < 99% (critical).
  * p99 latency increased > 3x baseline and p95 > 2x baseline.
  * 5xx rate increased by > 200% absolute and accounts for > 0.5% of traffic.
  * Model eval score drop > 3% relative on golden prompt set.
- Pause and reduce ramp if observed for 5 consecutive 1m windows:
  * Success rate between 99% and 99.8% with rising 4xxs.
  * Queue time increases > 30% and autoscaler not keeping up.
- Soft-alert (watch closely) when:
  * Cost per token increases > 20% but no user-visible degradation.

Stakeholders and on-call roles:
- Launch lead (product-ops): Emily Carter — coordinates decisions and communications.
- SRE on-call: primary pager — triage infra, scale, network.
- Serving runtime owner: Rajan Patel — model routing, cache invalidation, kernel fallbacks.
- ML lead (quality): Sofia Martinez — evaluate outputs and quality regressions.
- Customer success triage: Claire Huang — handle any early customer reports.

Pre-rollout checklist (must be green before Phase A):
- [ ] Canary environment matches prod config (env vars, secrets).
- [ ] Baseline benchmarks recorded for p50/p95/p99 and token throughput.
- [ ] Smoke test script (smoke/run_canary.sh) executed and passing.
- [ ] Dashboards deployed and bookmarked: TrafficShift / LaunchWatch / ModelQuality.
- [ ] Alert routing configured (Slack #launch-watch, PagerDuty policy).
- [ ] Rollback artifact and previous model pinned and fast-promote tested.
- [ ] Communication plan drafted (who, when, escalation steps).

Operational actions and run sequence:
1. Launch lead announces Phase A start in #launch-watch and triggers config change.
2. SRE verifies traffic flow and checks Success rate/Latency within 10m.
3. ML lead runs the golden prompt sampling check and reports pass/fail.
4. If PASS after 30m, proceed to Phase B; if not, follow circuit-breaker.

Escalation ladder (who to call and when):
- If failure meets 'Stop' criteria: Launch lead initiates rollback; SRE pauses traffic; notify CTO and Support within 5 minutes.
- If multiple non-critical anomalies: product-ops decides to pause ramp and consult runtime and ML owners.

Rollback checklist (on rollback decision):
- [ ] Trigger traffic redirect to previous variant (routing rule ID).
- [ ] Confirm consumer-facing success rate returns to baseline.
- [ ] Capture heap/stack/dump logs and correlate with timestamps.
- [ ] Open incident ticket and add timeline and metric snapshots.
- [ ] Conduct postmortem with stakeholders within 72 hours.

Measurement and artifacts to collect during rollout:
- 1m-resolution timeseries for success rate, p50/p95/p99 latency, queue length, cpu/gpu utilization.
- Sample of 200 model outputs (golden prompt set) at each phase for ML quality checks.
- Cost profile for the period (per-region) and per-token unit economics.
- A/B scoring snapshot for model quality dashboards.

Quick check templates (copy/paste for Slack):
- "Phase A start — canary at 1% for 30m. Monitoring: TrafficShift dashboard; SRE oncall: @pagerduty. Callout: if success_rate < 99% for 3m, rollback immediately."
- "Observability note — p95 increasing to {value}; queue rising — holding ramp. Need serving runtime confirmation."

Post-launch: 6-hour watch and 30-day health metrics to track
- Adoption signal: % users hitting new path, errors by cohort, model acceptance rate.
- Stability: weekly p99 distribution, tail-error analysis, rollout-induced regressions.
- Cost: 30-day rolling cost delta and efficiency actions.

Open questions & todo:
- Validate golden prompt set covers enterprise edge cases (assigned: Sofia).
- Add per-region circuit thresholds for APAC (assigned: Rajan).
- Automate rollback via playbook in infra pipeline (assigned: SRE team).

Notes and references:
- Link to LaunchWatch dashboard: (internal) /dashboards/launchwatch
- Jira tickets: PRODOPS-781 (traffic-shift infra), PRODOPS-789 (model-quality gating)
- GitHub: platform PR #1234 contains the routing change used for the canary.

Appendix: quick KPI table (for copy to sheet)
- Metric, baseline, stop_threshold, pause_threshold, owner
- success_rate, 99.95%, 99%, 99.8%, SRE
- p95_latency, 180ms, 540ms, 360ms, Product
- 5xx_rate, 0.05%, 0.5%, 0.2%, SRE
- eval_score_delta, 0%, -3%, -1.5%, ML

End of runbook. Keep this doc as the short operational reference and link to the longer launch playbooks for full communications and marketing readiness.
